content.text: This is a clear true positive - standard OWASP Benchmark XPath injection test case where user-controlled header value flows unsanitized into an XPath expression.

input.justification:
The value of the "BenchmarkTest01223" HTTP header is read via request.getHeaders(), URL-decoded, passed through a trivial pass-through helper method (Test.doSomething, which for switchTarget='A' just returns the param unchanged), and then concatenated directly into an XPath expression string ("/Employees/Employee[@emplid='" + bar + "']") that is compiled and evaluated with XPath.evaluate(). There is no sanitization, escaping, or validation of the value anywhere in the flow - only an XXE mitigation (disallow-doctype-decl) is applied, which does not address XPath injection. An attacker can supply a header value like `' or '1'='1` to manipulate the XPath query logic. This matches the classic XPath injection pattern and is a true positive.</justification>
